description: Cosmetic icon per serving-unit type. The vocabulary is closed and lives in pocket-nutrition-knowledge/serving_unit_types.yaml; this maps seven of its ten entries. shot, bowl and scoop have NO icon on purpose — no glyph reads unambiguously as any of them, and a wrong icon is worse than none — so `expected` is null for those, never an empty string. teaspoon and tablespoon deliberately share one glyph. An unknown unit outside the vocabulary also has none, so a client never needs a placeholder.

cases.why: The smallest unit in the vocabulary. Reachable in shortcut-profile only to be dropped as sub-gram, so its icon is never rendered there and would otherwise go unpinned.
Both spoons are 🥄. A port that keys one and forgets the other still passes shortcut-profile, which only ever asserts one of them per case.
The other half of the shared glyph, asserted separately so neither can be dropped.
The one unit whose icon differs from the spoons in the shortcut-profile cases, which is why that suite catches a swapped pair but not a missing third entry.
Unreachable from any shortcut-profile case, so entirely unpinned before this suite.
The underscored key. A port that camel-cases vocabulary keys breaks here and nowhere else.
The volumetric unit a drink resolves to; unpinned before this suite.
In the vocabulary, deliberately unmapped. Distinguishes "no glyph chosen" from "unit not known", which a client must treat identically.
Also in the vocabulary and also unmapped. 🥣 is already the cup, and reusing it would make two different units render the same.
The unit shortcut-profile uses for its unknown-unit case. It is in the vocabulary, so that case pins the unmapped path rather than the unknown-unit path — a distinction worth making explicit here.
Knowledge could add a unit before this map does. The result is a missing icon, never a placeholder and never an error.
